'''Shark fin soup''' is a soup or stewed dish served in parts of [[China]], [[Taiwan]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=[[Saeed Kamali Dehghan]]|date=2019-06-04|title=Marine 'gold rush': demand for shark fin soup drives decimation of fish|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2019/jun/04/marine-gold-rush-demand-shark-fin-soup|access-date=2021-07-14|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=[[Adam Sweeting]]|date=2011-01-17|title=Gordon Ramsay: Shark Bait/ Dispatches: Fish Unwrapped, Channel 4|url=https://theartsdesk.com/tv/gordon-ramsay-shark-bait-dispatches-fish-unwrapped-channel-4|website=[[The Arts Desk]]|language=en|access-date=14 July 2021|archive-date=14 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210714103824/https://theartsdesk.com/tv/gordon-ramsay-shark-bait-dispatches-fish-unwrapped-channel-4|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Southeast Asia]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Simon Denyer|date=2018|title=Even as China turns away from shark fin soup, the prestige dish is gaining popularity elsewhere in Asia|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2018/02/14/even-as-china-turns-away-from-shark-fin-soup-the-prestige-dish-is-gaining-popularity-elsewhere-in-asia/|archive-date=20 June 2021|access-date=14 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620102116/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2018/02/14/even-as-china-turns-away-from-shark-fin-soup-the-prestige-dish-is-gaining-popularity-elsewhere-in-asia/|url-status=live}}</ref> The shark fins provide texture, while the taste comes from the other ingredients.<ref name="NYT Bradsher"/> As one of the [[four sea delicacies]], it is commonly served at special occasions such as weddings and banquets, or as a [[luxury item]].<ref name="NYT Bradsher">Keith Bradsher, [https://www.nytimes.com/2005/06/17/business/worldbusiness/disneyland-in-china-offers-a-soup-and-lands-in-a-stew.html Disneyland in China Offers a Soup and Lands in a Stew] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151114231622/http://www.nytimes.com/2005/06/17/business/worldbusiness/disneyland-in-china-offers-a-soup-and-lands-in-a-stew.html |date=14 November 2015 }}, 17 June 2005 ''[[The New York Times]]''</ref>

It has been condemned by the [[Humane Society International]], which states that approximately 72 million sharks are killed each year for their fins.<ref>[http://www.hsi.org/issues/shark_finning/ Shark Finning] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725035910/http://www.hsi.org/issues/shark_finning/ |date=25 July 2010 }}. [[Humane Society International]].</ref> Currently, international concerns over the [[sustainable seafood|sustainability]] and [[animal welfare|welfare]] of sharks have impacted consumption and availability of the soup worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/in-china-victory-for-wildlife-conservation-as-citizens-persuaded-to-give-up-shark-fin-soup/2013/10/19/e8181326-3646-11e3-89db-8002ba99b894_print.html|title=In China, victory for wildlife conservation as citizens persuaded to give up shark fin soup - The Washington Post|website=www.washingtonpost.com|access-date=20 January 2017|archive-date=16 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116230158/https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/in-china-victory-for-wildlife-conservation-as-citizens-persuaded-to-give-up-shark-fin-soup/2013/10/19/e8181326-3646-11e3-89db-8002ba99b894_print.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Recently, health concerns about the high concentration of [[BMAA]] in shark fins have arisen.

Shark fin soup substitutes have lately appeared on the market which do not require any shark fins.<ref>{{cite web |title=Faux Fins And Mock Meat: Is Clean Meat The Answer To Reforming Shark Fin And Foie Gras? |website=[[Forbes]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928234510/https://www.forbes.com/sites/lesliewu/2018/07/30/faux-fins-and-mock-meat-is-clean-meat-the-answer-to-reforming-shark-fin-and-foie-gras/ |archive-date=2022-09-28 |url-status=live |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/lesliewu/2018/07/30/faux-fins-and-mock-meat-is-clean-meat-the-answer-to-reforming-shark-fin-and-foie-gras/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://thefuturemarket.com/faux-fin |title=Alpha Food Lab Faux fin |access-date=17 March 2021 |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628021054/https://thefuturemarket.com/faux-fin |url-status=live }}</ref>
